summary: Hegoda Khemananda worked in Buddhist studies. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her Dr. Polit. at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006) under Signe Howell, later serving there as a postdoctoral fellow (~2007–2010).
Heidi I. Köppl works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi Pauwels specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, University of Cologne, and University of Washington (PhD 1994, under Alan W. Entwistle), she held posts at SOAS (1994–1996) and University of Washington (1996–2009).

Heike Oberlin specializes in Indology. She studied at Kerala Kalamandalam, the University of Würzburg (PhD), and the University of Tübingen (MA, Habilitation), where she held academic posts (2005–2008), alongside appointments at Kerala Kalamandalam (2018) and the University of Rome (2025).

Heiner Eichner was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1964–1974) and held a post at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
Heinrich August Jäschke was a linguist and Tibetologist. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky (1847) and as a Moravian missionary in Kyelang and the Moravian Church from 1856/1857 to 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann was a scholar of Iranian, Indological, and historical studies. He studied at Leipzig, Paris, and Calcutta, and held posts at Aliah University (assistant professor 1860, 1870; principal 1865), Doveton College (1862–1864), and The Asiatic Society (1868).
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1839–1843) and held a post at the University of Munich (~1865–1894).

Heinrich Ewald worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. After earning his Promotion at the University of Göttingen (1820–1823), he held professorships at Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

Heinrich Hettrich specialized in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Saarland University, University of Giessen, and University of Munich, he held posts at Saarland, Marburg, and Würzburg, and led the Society for Indo-European Studies (1996–2008).

Heinrich Hübschmann was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Indology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, Munich (PhD under Martin Haug), and Leipzig, and held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1876) and the University of Strasbourg (1877).

Heinrich Kiepert was a scholar of history, archaeology, and geography. Educated at the University of Berlin and Jena (Dr. phil.), he headed the geography department at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir (1845–1852) and became ordinary professor of geography at the University of Berlin in 1874.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer worked in linguistics and oriental studies. Educated at the University of Leipzig and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy, he held the chair for Oriental Languages at Leipzig from 1836 and co-founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Munich and Göttingen (PhD under Franz Kielhorn), he held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and the University of Berlin (chair 1909–1935), also heading the Prussian Academy's Oriental Commission.

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Berlin (~1884–1885) and Strasbourg (~1885–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and the University of Heidelberg (~1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1845–1852) and the University of Breslau (~1852–1875).
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in ~1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe, serving there from 1841 to 1889 as Ordinarius for Sanskrit and comparative linguistics.
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig, studying under Hermann Brockhaus. He taught classical languages at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.
